chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of his companions, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Saqafi, from Ibrahim ibn Yahya al-Thawri, from Haysam ibn Bashir, from Abu Bashir, from Abu Rawh,

that a woman disguised herself as a slave girl for a man, and that was at night, so he had intercourse with her while he thought she was his slave girl. The matter was raised to Umar, so he sent to Ali (peace be upon him), who said: 'Strike the man with a penalty (hadd) in secret, and strike the woman with a penalty (hadd) in public.'

key_terms.عَلِيٍّ ( عليه السلام ): Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)
key_terms.فَوَاقَعَهَا: so he had intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man having intercourse with a woman who disguised herself as his slave?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the jurisprudential nuance in applying *hadd* penalties based on social status and the context of the act. Ali ibn Abi Talib’s ruling distinguishes between the man, who is punished in secret (*fi al-sirr*) due to his likely higher status or the private nature of the encounter, and the woman, who is punished in public (*fi al-'alaniyah*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on modesty and the specific circumstances of the parties involved. This case is often cited by scholars to discuss the discretion (*ra'y*) of the Imam in legal judgments and the distinction between *zina* (unmarried) and *zina bil-jabr* or other forms depending on interpretation.
